铁蛋 ("iron egg") is a genuine, warm rustic nickname wishing toughness/durability on a child - reads as affectionate, not mocking. Good fit for a tough little mud creature.

二狗 ("Second Dog") is an authentic ultra-rustic Chinese nickname pattern. On a person today it can read as a bit of a hillbilly joke, but for a small, deliberately ugly-endearing mud frog the goofy, unpretentious flavor actually fits the brief well and reads as affectionate-in-context rather than a put-down. "Doggo" is a loose but fitting gloss.

Big Sturdy reads awkwardly as an English name (two stacked adjectives); a single word like "Sturdy" matches the house style (cf. Chunky, Chubby, Dopey) and is still accurate. 大壮 itself is a genuine, warm rustic nickname, no connotation issue.
Blackie is accurate for 小黑 (a very common real nickname for a black pet) but reads as dated/racially loaded in English. Suggest a neutral color-based gloss like "Shadow" instead.

阿土 ("Ah-Tu") follows a genuine warm Southern-Chinese naming pattern (阿+character). 土 can mean "unsophisticated/bumpkin," but in this affectionate 阿- form it reads as fond self-deprecating humor, fitting an earthy mud creature, not an insult.
